name: Moped
description: A two- or three-wheeler whose motor, electric or combustion, produces 2 horsepower (1,500 W) or less and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground, with an automatic drive. Defined by Hawaii Revised Statutes §286-2 and §291C-1, as amended by HB 2021 (Act 259, 2026); Act 222 (2025) raised the minimum age to 16 and requires a helmet at every age.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and a direct or automatic drive that needs no clutch or gear shifting
Its motor produces 2 horsepower (1,500 W) or less at the output shaft; a combustion engine is also limited to 50 cc
Can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground; one that can is a motor-driven cycle instead
A bicycle whose motor exceeds an electric bicycle's 750 W but stays within these limits meets this definition; an unregistered one over 750 W that can exceed 28 mph is a high-speed electric device
Must carry the manufacturer's label certifying it meets federal motor vehicle safety standards to be registered
Registered every year with the county director of finance for $27, with a plate on the rear, and must pass an annual safety inspection
Riders must be 16 or older and carry a driver's license of any class, including the moped-only Class 1, or an instruction permit
Every rider must wear a safety helmet fastened with a chin strap, at any age, since June 25, 2025
Ridden seated astride and facing forward, with no passenger, except a three-wheeled moped with side-by-side seats
No insurance required for a two-wheeled moped; a three-wheeled one must carry liability and property damage coverage
May not be driven faster than 35 mph; a three-wheeled moped is limited to roads posted 35 mph or less
Not allowed on freeways, sidewalks or pedestrian paths, and since July 15, 2026 barred from bike lanes, bike paths and any path or roadway designated for bicycles
